summary: Controlled saved-views UI for data toolbars, including selection, dirty state, create, save, discard, rename, remove, validation, and focus behavior without owning view configuration or persistence.
useWhen: A data view lets people recall and manage named combinations of filters, sorting, grouping, and presentation preferences.
Several products need the same saved-view interaction while retaining different view payloads and storage systems.
avoidWhen: The choices do not represent restorable view configurations.
The application expects the component to serialize filters, grouping, sorting, columns, pagination, or product-specific state.
accessibility: The primary control retains combobox semantics and exposes a direct accessible name.
Each custom view exposes a separately named options trigger. The options menu supports keyboard navigation and returns focus through the shared Select and Menu behavior.

The naming dialog traps focus through Modal behavior. The dialog heading names the task, so the name field omits a visible label; the input keeps aria-label Name, Field associates validation text, and focus returns to the saved-views control after closing.
Footer actions are assigned with slot="footer" on each button so Modal owns the two-action layout.
states: views, value, and dirty are controlled. Dirty state is presented only for a selected custom view; the default template never shows the trigger dot or save/discard actions even if dirty is supplied. Selection, create, save, discard, rename, and remove events communicate intent and never mutate application records.
The component owns only transient interaction state: the contextual menu, naming dialog, draft name, duplicate-name validation, and focus restoration.

The default view is a non-editable template. Application-owned custom views appear in a separate section with Rename and Remove actions. New view opens the naming dialog. When an editable selected view is dirty, that view row shows Save and negative Discard supporting actions while the footer remains dedicated to New view. The application decides which view state to capture, restore, and persist.
The built-in picker and contextual option menu each retain their own surface-open treatment. Opening a view menu does not select that view.
Borderless toolbar compositions omit resting control borders while retaining focus and interaction feedback.
Expanded toolbar triggers use an icon and regular-weight text without a trailing chevron.
Selected views and applied filters do not promote trigger icon or label colors. Trigger colors remain neutral across value changes.
responsiveBehavior: The control remains a single toolbar item and relies on Select, Menu, and Modal collision and viewport behavior. Its trigger hugs short view names and is capped at the compact menu-width token so long names truncate while the dirty dot stays visible. Its choice popup keeps that same token as the minimum width.
Place it in the start region of ds-data-toolbar so the middle region can keep left-side and right-side controls on one spanning cluster.
The ViewMenu prefix identifies saved views. Compact compositions, narrow table captions, and narrow standalone data toolbars show only the icon while retaining the accessible name and tooltip.

customElements: Assign views through the JavaScript property and update value after handling dsViewChange.
react: Keep view records and serialized view configuration in application state; update controlled props in response to the component events.
angular: Import the generated DsDataSavedViews adapter and bind views, value, and dirty; handle event.detail for selection and mutations.
